fields.features_heading: What a Supplier Needs to Quote Without a Call
fields.features_subheading: An RFQ form defines the item so every supplier prices the same thing. These six parts cover the lines and the answers that come back.
fields.feature_1:
A unit of measure on every line

Each line carries a part number, a quantity, and a unit picked from a list: each, foot, box, or case. A line with no unit will not submit. That leaves 300 meaning one thing.
fields.feature_2:
Drawings filed on the line they describe

Attach a drawing or a data sheet to the line it belongs to. The supplier opens the RFQ and finds each file beside its part number instead of in a separate email thread.
fields.feature_3:
One response sheet for every supplier

Each invited supplier gets its own link to the same fields: unit price, freight, lead time in days, and the date the quote expires. Answers arrive as rows you can sort.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders before the RFQ closes

Set a closing date and time. Two days before it, suppliers who have not answered get an email reminder, and the buyer sees which suppliers have replied and which have gone quiet.
fields.feature_5:
Each request routed to whoever prices it

Send each incoming RFQ by order size or product line. Large orders can reach a senior estimator in Slack, while the small ones join the inside sales queue by email instead.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository, then connect the form to your ERP or host it on your own servers. Keep building on the app from there.

fields.usecase_heading: Who Sends an RFQ, and Who Answers It
fields.tab_content_1:
All 12 lines arrive with a unit attached

Ilona Vasko buys for Stannard Electric, and a clinic fit-out needs 12 lines quoted by Fenmoor Electric Supply. Line 4 asked for 300 of EMT conduit with no unit. The form held it until she picked feet over 10-foot sticks. Emeka Ruthven in inside sales got the RFQ with a unit on every line.
fields.tab_content_2:
The cheapest can loses by $330 once freight is in

Pipewell Cider needs 120,000 16-ounce cans and sent one RFQ to three suppliers. Each answered the same sheet, with freight on its own line. Brightmet Containers had the lowest can at $0.131, but $1,650 in freight brought it to $17,370 delivered. Norrland Packaging won at $17,040, freight included.
fields.tab_content_3:
Over 6 pallets, it goes to Ksenia on truckload

Ambergate Furniture asked Sorrel Line Logistics to quote 8 pallets weighing 6,400 lb from Grand Rapids to Denver, with a liftgate at delivery. Requests over 6 pallets skip the less-than-truckload (LTL) queue. This one reached Ksenia Darrow on the truckload desk by email, with the lane and the liftgate note at the top.
fields.tab_content_4:
Two suppliers split six lines, and the third hears why

Six lines went out in one janitorial RFQ from Linden Valley Health. Hedda Moorcroft gave each line to its lowest price: lines 1 to 4 to Clearbrook Sanitary for $6,240, and lines 5 and 6 to Hollis Paper Supply for $1,980. Marlpit Distributors got an email saying it ranked second on all 6 lines.

fields.howto_title: How to Make an RFQ Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build an RFQ form that gets every supplier pricing the same items on the same terms.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the items before you write a field
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Match each unit to how you stock it
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Pick the terms a quote must carry
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Write the award rule on the form
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull every line from the drawing or the last order, with a part number and a quantity for each. Where a substitute is acceptable, add "or equal" to the line. A supplier then knows it may quote an alternative instead of guessing.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick the unit you count and pay in for each line, such as feet for wire and each for boxes. If a supplier sells by the case of 12, ask for its pack size on the response sheet and convert before you compare prices.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Beyond price, choose the terms you will weigh, such as payment terms or a warranty period. Make each one a required answer. No quote comes back missing the one term that decides the award.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Say how you will choose before anyone prices: lowest delivered total, or each line to its own lowest bid. Put the rule in the RFQ itself. Every supplier reads the same terms, and a losing bidder can see why.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Get a contact for every supplier
fields.howto_step_5_des: Collect a contact name and email for every invited supplier rather than a general sales inbox. Reminders and award emails then reach someone who can answer, and a late reply has a name attached to chase.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Set the sort before quotes arrive
fields.howto_step_6_des: Choose the column that ranks the quotes: unit price, delivered total with freight, or lead time in days. Set it now. The table is ready to read the morning the RFQ closes.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Describe it to Emergent and test
fields.howto_step_7_des: Paste your lines, answer fields and closing date into a prompt, and Emergent builds the form and its database. Send a test RFQ to a colleague with one line missing its unit, and check that it stops before it sends.

faq_plan.a: An RFQ form is the document a buyer uses to request a quote from a supplier for specific products or services. It lists each item with its specification, which keeps every supplier bidding on the same thing. Good RFQ forms also fix the answer fields, and the replies line up for comparison.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an RFQ form?
faq_plan.a: Describe the items, the answer fields, and the closing date to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English. Emergent builds the form, the supplier response sheet, and the database behind them. Change any field later by asking for it in the same chat.

faq_plan.q: What should an RFQ form template include?
faq_plan.a: An RFQ form template needs a line for each item with its quantity and unit, plus the fields every supplier must fill in. Ask for unit price, freight, and lead time, plus contract length when the deal runs past one order. Close with a submission deadline and the name of the buyer who answers questions.

faq_plan.q: Is there a standard RFQ form?
faq_plan.hint: What is the standard RFQ form?
faq_plan.a: For US federal buying, yes: the FAR prescribes SF 18 for obtaining price, cost, delivery, and related information from suppliers. Under the FAR, a quotation is not an offer and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. For private buying, write your own, and use a proposal form for work you want designed.

faq_plan.q: What unit of measure goes on each line of an RFQ form?
faq_plan.hint: What is uom on RFQ form?
faq_plan.a: Use the unit you count the item in when it arrives and sits on the shelf. A unit of measure is the unit in which an item's quantity is managed, such as each, a box of 12 or a case of 144. Write it on every line, because 300 of conduit can mean feet or sticks.

faq_plan.q: How do I compare supplier quotes from an RFQ form?
faq_plan.a: Compare on the delivered total, not the unit price: add freight and any setup charge to each quote before you rank them. Then check lead time against your need date and drop any quote that misses it. The app Emergent builds keeps every supplier's answers as rows in a database you own. The comparison becomes a sort, not a spreadsheet you retype.

faq_plan.q: Can one RFQ form handle different kinds of requests?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the form branches on the first answer: goods get item lines with units, and services get a scope and a schedule. Keep requests that are not purchases on their own form, such as a sponsorship form for an event partner. Mixing them makes each supplier wade through fields that do not apply.

faq_plan.q: How many suppliers should get the same RFQ form?
faq_plan.a: Send the same RFQ form to at least three suppliers when the market has three who can deliver. Add a fourth for any line where a supplier has declined to quote before. A form Emergent builds has no response caps, and every invited supplier answers through its own link.

faq_plan.q: Should RFQ forms ask suppliers how long a quote stays valid?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Make the expiry date a required answer, and ask for at least as many days as your approval takes. A quote that lapses while the order waits for sign-off has to be priced again. The app Emergent builds can email the buyer a reminder before the earliest quote expires.

faq_plan.q: When does a purchase need proposals instead of an RFQ form?
faq_plan.a: Ask for proposals when you cannot specify the item well enough for suppliers to price the same thing. RFQs are best suited to products and services that are as standardized as possible, which makes each quote comparable. For work where the supplier designs the approach, collect answers on your rfp form and score them.

plan.angle: The live top 10 splits two ways: request-a-quote forms that suppliers put on their own sites (a WordPress plugin tutorial, two form-template sites, a freight forwarder and an equipment maker) and public-sector RFQ packets (a city's federal attachments, a state DOT matrix, a planning agency's submission form). None of them handles what makes an RFQ hard: a unit of measure on every line, the same answer fields for every supplier, freight priced so totals compare, and an award split by line. This page answers what an RFQ form is and what a standard one holds, then shows both sides using a live form: a distributor receiving a contractor's line-item RFQ, a cidery comparing can quotes on landed cost, a freight broker routing a lane request by pallet count, and a hospital buyer awarding lines to two suppliers. Proposals stay on the rfp form sibling and supplier price requests for one job stay on the quote form sibling.

findings.quote: For US federal buying, yes: the FAR prescribes SF 18 for obtaining price, cost, delivery, and related information from suppliers. Under the FAR, a quotation is not an offer and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract.
findings.issue: Source scope dropped (rework checklist 2). FAR 53.213 sits under 'Simplified acquisition procedures' and prescribes SF 18 'as specified in 13.307(b)', adding that 'SF 1449 ... or other agency forms/automated formats, may also be used'; FAR 13.004 is likewise a Part 13 (simplified acquisition) rule. The answer says 'For US federal buying, yes' and 'Under the FAR', presenting SF 18 as the single standard form for all federal buying and the not-an-offer rule as FAR-wide. The writer's own domain_sources claim says 'In US federal simplified acquisitions'. Both sentences in FAQ 4 carry this; no other field mentions the FAR or SF 18.
findings.fix: Scope both sentences to simplified acquisitions and keep the alternative: e.g. 'For US federal simplified acquisitions, the FAR prescribes SF 18, Request for Quotations, though SF 1449 or an agency's own form may also be used. In those buys, a quotation is not an offer, so the Government cannot accept it to form a binding contract.' Keep the private-buying sentence as advice. Stay within 75 words.
